Indicate the lookback time for duplicate checking. This item stores the string value of the duplicate interval (in days). This value is converted into hours and populated into item-17220 Inpatient Duplicate Interval. To specify an interval in DAYS, you can enter a positive number. To specify an interval in HOURS, you can enter it in terms of days. (e.g., to specify 6 hours, enter .25) To specify the interval in weeks, you can enter a number/fraction followed by the letter W. (e.g., to specify 3 weeks, type 3W or 3.0W). The value is converted to equivalent days and displayed to the user. Note: Large interval values may cause the system to slow down considerably. Please consult your system Technical Services Representative before setting large values in this field. When a procedure is ordered, a check is made to see if that procedure had been previously ordered within the duplicate interval. If found, the user is asked whether to continue placing the order.

The origin type of exchange coverages.

The date the member on the coverage was last verified.

The date on which the member applied for coverage.
The time on which the member applied for coverage.

The state of the member's custodial parent.

The member's sex as it is recorded in the payor's system.

The category value associated with the relationship of the patient to the guarantor.

The member scheduled discontinuation date.
If the member is a full time student this column contains the value “Y”. If the member is not a full time student, as determined by the member’s Employment Status, this column contains the value “N”.
The reason the member was terminated from the coverage.
The last saved value of the member's verification status.
The verification record for the coverage member.
The member ID received on the source file for the member on the coverage.
This item stores the member's date of birth as it is recorded in the payer's system.
The ID of the user who last verified this member's status.

This column contains a number representing the number of business (non-weekend, non-holiday) days since 1850-01-01. This column will take into consideration holidays that are set at the Service Area or Location level, but not those set at the Department level.
The date in normal date format.
The date formatted as a string, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
This is the "day" part of the date only. For example, if the date is May 13, this column contains "13".

The category number of the day of the week. The values in this column start at 0 for Thursday and end at 6 for Wednesday. You can join to this column from day of the week columns based on ZC_DAY_OF_THE_WEEK, or with a Format INI of "SCH" and a Format Item of "130".   If the other column is based on ZC_WHICH_DAYS or has a Format INI of "ECT" and a Format Item of "710", use WHICH_DAYS_C instead.
Monday, Tuesday, etc.

Contains a number representing the day of the week in the current locale for the corresponding CALENDAR_DT. The first day of the week is 0 and the last day of the week is 6.  For example, Sunday is the first day of the week in the United States. So Sunday would be 0 and Saturday would be 6 in this column.
This column contains the Nth day of the year. For example, January 1 will be day 1 and December 31 will normally be day 365.
Much of the date information stored in the OLTP system is in an integer format known as DAT. The DAT is equal to 121531-DTE. The DAT decreases as time goes on. This column contains the DAT.
The OLTP database stores some dates in an internal integer format known as the DTE. The DTE increases as time goes on. This column contains the DTE.
Indicates whether the date is a holiday. "Y" represents that the date is a holiday, otherwise a value of "N" will appear. Depends on the locale definition.

Much of the datetime information in the OLTP system is stored in a format that represents a numeric number of seconds called an Instant. This column contains the Instant of a particular day at 12AM. The ACCESS_LOG tables have an indexed (PK) column that is in this format.

The last occurrence that month of the last business day of the week.  This may or may not be a Friday, depending on the locale definition.  Used to help determine the last full business week of the month.
This column shows whether this year is a leap year.
The first day of the month for the date in datetime format.
The first day of the month as a string, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
This is the last day of the month. For example, 02/28/2007.
Indicates whether or not the date in this row is the last day of a month.  This is frequently used as a filter and should be used instead of comparing CALENDAR_DT to MONTH_END_DT.
The month name in long form. For example, "February".
The month in integer form. For example, February will be "2".
This column contains the month and year in 'MonthName YYYY' format. For example, if the CALENDAR_DT is 2012-01-31, this column would display 'January 2012'.
This column tells you how many times a particular day of the week has occurred in the given month. Use this column to find--for example--the fourth Tuesday of the month.
This is the previous day's date.
The first day of the quarter formatted as a string, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
This date is the first day of the quarter.
This date is the last day of the quarter.
This column contains the yearly quarter number in integer form. For example, February is in Quarter 1 while November is in Quarter 4.
This column contains the quarter number as a string in the format 'Q#'.
This column returns the date of a year ago. If CALENDAR_DT=2/24/2009, then this column will return 2/24/2008. If CALENDAR_DT is Feb. 29th, then this column returns nothing.
This is the date of the next day. Use this column to help linking datetime values. For example, CONTACT_DATE>=CALENDAR_DT and CONTACT_DT<TOMORROW_DT

This column contains the first date of the United States federal fiscal year.  The U.S. federal fiscal year currently begins on 1 October and ends on 30 September.  The current fiscal year went into effect on 1 October 1976; this column is not accurate for dates prior to 1 October 1976.

This column contains the last date of the United States federal fiscal year.  The U.S. federal fiscal year currently begins on 1 October and ends on 30 September.  The current fiscal year went into effect on 1 October 1976; this column is not accurate for dates prior to 1 October 1976.
The first day of the week in datetime format.
The first day of the week as a string, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
The last day of the week in normal date format. Depends on the locale definition.
The number of the week in the year. Depends on the locale definition.
This column contains a number representing the number of weekdays since 1850-01-01. This column does not take holidays into consideration.
Contains "Y" for weekend days. Otherwise, contains "N". Depends on the locale definition.

The category number of the day of the week. The values in this column start at 1 for Sunday and end at 7 for Saturday. You can join to this column from day of the week columns based on ZC_WHICH_DAYS, or with a Format INI of "ECT" and a Format Item of "710".   If the other column is based on ZC_DAY_OF_THE_WEEK or has a Format INI of "SCH" and a Format Item of "130", use DAY_OF_THE_WEEK_C instead.
This column contains the four-digit year.
The first day of the year for the date in datetime format.
The first day of the year as a string, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
The last date of the year for the CALENDAR_DT.
To help group by month, this column contains the month and year. The format is YYYYMM.
This column contains the year and month number as a string in the format 'YYYY-MM'.

The four-digit year that the WEEK_NUMBER corresponds to.  Depending on where in the week the new year starts and the locale definition, this may be the year before or after the actual date.  For instance, December 31st may be considered part of the first week of the following year.
This column contains the year and quarter information in the format 'YYYY Q#'.
The unique ID of the ADT event in which the patient was transferred, admitted, or returned from a leave of absence to this department.

Whether MyChart Bedside was activated during the admission and coinciding department visit. This will be 1 if an activation occurred while the patient was in the current department, and 0 otherwise. There can be only one MyChart Bedside activation per admission. This column may not be reliably set if you do not use Epic's Grand Central application.
The instant a patient or proxy first used a MyChart Bedside tablet to access this admission, in local time.

If the patient had a central line any time within the 48 hours prior to the event time of the bloodstream infection, this column will be 1. Otherwise, it will be 0. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

If the documentation in the patient's chart indicates that a bloodstream infection occurred during the hospital stay, this column will have the value 1. Otherwise, it will have the value 0. This is populated through the problem class for Problem List documentation and the present-on-admission field in the final diagnoses section of the HB Coding activity. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

If the documentation in the patient's chart indicates that the patient was infected with a bloodstream infection within the duration of stay on this patient day, then this column stores the date and time of the infection. Otherwise, this column is null. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

If the patient had an umbilical line any time within the 48 hours prior to the event time of the bloodstream infection, this column will be 1. Otherwise, it will be 0. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.
The date of this patient day in normal date format.

If the patient was in this department at the census instant, then the column displays the census time on that day. If the census time falls outside of the associated ADT event on that day, this column is null.

If the patient was on a central line at the census instant, then this flag will have the value 1. Otherwise, it will have the value 0. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

The number of nonviolent restraints episodes with fully compliant documentation that began in the department associated with this patient day. A restraint has fully compliant documentation if all flowsheet documentation associated with it was documented correctly.

The number of violent restraints episodes with fully compliant documentation that began in the department associated with this patient day. A restraint has fully compliant documentation if all flowsheet documentation associated with it was documented correctly.
The unique ID of the department that the patient was in during this patient day.

This column is only used to map departments to the department groupers. If null, then the department does not belong to any of the department groupers listed under property values. If not null, the value is translated in the following way:  1 - Critical Care 2 - Medical-Surgical Combined 3 - Medical
The number of minutes the patient spent in the department associated with this patient day.
The number of falls documented for the patient within the duration of stay on this patient day.
The instant when the patient was admitted or transferred to the department.
The unique ID of the Inpatient Data Store record of the patient associated with this patient day.
The number of nonviolent restraints episodes that began in the department associated with this patient day.
The number of minutes the patient spent on nonviolent restraints in the department associated with this patient day. This number does not include time spent only in seclusion.
The instant when the patient was transferred out of the department or discharged. If the patient was still in this department as of the extract time, this will be null.
The unique contact serial number for this contact. This number is unique across all patient encounters in your system. If you use IntraConnect, this is the Unique Contact Identifier (UCI).
The unique ID of the patient associated with this patient day. This column is frequently used to link to the PATIENT table.

If the documentation in the patient's chart indicates that he or she acquired pneumonia during the hospital stay, then this column will have the value 1.  Otherwise, it will have the value 0.  This is populated through the problem class for Problem List documentation and the present-on-admission field in the final diagnoses section of the HB Coding activity. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

If the documentation in the patient's chart indicates that the patient was infected with pneumonia within the duration of stay on this patient day, then this column stores the date and time of the infection. Otherwise, this column is null. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

If the patient was on a ventilator any time within the 48 hours prior to the event time of pneumonia, this column will be 1. Otherwise, it will be 0. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.  F_VENT_EPISODES must be configured for this column to populate.

Whether MyChart Bedside was activated in a prior department visit during the admission. This will be 1 if an activation occurred while the patient was in a prior department, and 0 otherwise. This column may not be reliably set if you do not use Epic's Grand Central application.

If the patient was on an umbilical line at the census instant, then this flag will have the value 1. Otherwise, it will have the value 0. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

If the patient was on an indwelling urinary catheter at the census instant, then this flag will have the value 1. Otherwise, it will have the value 0. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

If the documentation in the patient's chart indicates that a urinary tract infection occurred during the hospital stay, this column will have the value 1. Otherwise, it will have the value 0. This is populated through the problem class for Problem List documentation and the present-on-admission field in the final diagnoses section of the HB Coding activity. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

If the documentation in the patient's chart indicates that the patient was infected with a urinary tract infection within the duration of stay on this patient day, then this column stores the date and time of the infection. Otherwise, this column is null. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

If the patient had a urinary catheter any time within the 48 hours prior to the event time of the urinary tract infection, this column will be 1. Otherwise, it will be 0. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.

If the patient was on mechanical ventilation at the census instant, then this flag will have the value 1. Otherwise, it will have the value 0. This column will not be populated if P_REPORT_ON_INFECTIONS_YN is set to 'No'.  F_VENT_EPISODES must be configured for this column to populate.
The number of violent restraints episodes that began in the department associated with this patient day.
The number of minutes the patient spent on violent restraints in the department associated with this patient day. This number does not include time spent only in seclusion.
The unique ID of the visit account associated with the appointment.
This column stores the time by which a patient should arrive for his or her appointment.
The category number for the block in which the appointment was schedule.
The date that the appointment was canceled, if it was canceled. This is the value in the APPT_CANC_DTTM column at midnight.
The date and time the appointment was canceled, in the local time zone of the primary appointment department.
The unique ID of the user who canceled the appointment.
The UTC date and time that the appointment was canceled.
The date and time that the appointment was confirmed.
The category number of the confirmation status for the appointment.
The unique ID associated with the user record that confirmed the appointment. This column is frequently used to link to the CLARITY_EMP table.
The date and time of the appointment, stored in the time zone of the appointment department. Use APPT_UTC_DTTM to get the time in UTC.
The unique ID of the user who made the appointment.
The total scheduled length of the appointment in minutes.

The date on which the appointment was made. This stores the same date as the APPT_MADE_DTTM column, but at midnight. Note that this may not store the same value as PAT_ENC.APPT_MADE_DATE. PAT_ENC.APPT_MADE_DATE may change when the appointment is changed, but the value of this column stays the same, and is thus what you should use when determining the date on which an appointment was entered in the system.
The date and time that the appointment was made.

The date and time that the appointment was made, stored in UTC. To get the time in the time zone of the user who created it, use APPT_MADE_DTTM.  This column will not be populated for appointments created prior to Epic 2012.
The category number of the application that performed the initial scheduling action on this appointment.
The appointment serial number for the appointment. This value is unique among appointments that are not canceled, and can be used to group together canceled and rescheduled appointments.
The category number of the appointment status.
The date and time of the appointment, in UTC. Use APPT_DTTM to get the date and time of the appointment in the appointment department's time zone.
The date and time of the system-audited removal from arrival list action.

The date and time when the first check-in began. If a user cancels out of the check-in workflow this field will not be populated. Also, if a user cancels check-in this field will be cleared.  This column is only populated for Hyperspace checkins through the scheduling application. It does not get populated for check-ins performed in Text, Welcome or via an automatic process such as through Cadence end of day processing.
The category number for the appointment cancellation reason if the appointment was canceled.
The number of times that an appointment has been changed. If an appointment has not been changed, this will be 0.
The encounter form number or charge slip number assigned to this appointment.
The unique ID of the workstation record for the check-in kiosk.
The unique ID of the workstation record for the check-out kiosk.

The date and time of the system-audited check-in.  If a check-in was canceled or the appointment was checked in multiple times, this column will store the time of the first check-in action after the last cancel check-in action. If there was a cancel check-in action without a subsequent check-in action, this column will be null. This may or may not be more accurate than the user-editable time recorded by the CHECKIN_TIME column in PAT_ENC.

The date and time of the system-audited check-out.   If the check-out was canceled, this column will store the time of the first check-out action after the last cancel check-out action. If there was a cancel check-out action without a subsequent check-out action, this column will be null. This may or may not be more accurate than the user-editable time recorded by the CHECKOUT_TIME column in PAT_ENC.
ID of the deployment owner for this contact.

Indicates whether or not the user overrode a warning that the patient chronically no-shows and should be booked in an overbook opening. Y indicates that the warning was overridden. N indicates that no such warning was displayed and overridden.
The date of the appointment. This stores the same date as the APPT_DTTM column, but at midnight.
The total copay collected for the visit.

The dollar amount in the Copay Due field on scheduling system’s Check In Patient window. This field may be calculated by the Benefit Engine or entered or modified by the user. It is a dollar amount field and may be NULL if no copay was recorded at Check In.
The unique ID of the user who collected the copay. If copay was collected multiple times, this stores the ID of the first copay collection user.

Indicates whether the appointment for this patient could have been scheduled online through Direct Scheduling. Yes (11) indicates the appointment would have been available, No (12) means it wouldn't have been available, Not Applicable (13) means the appointment didn't meet qualifications to check, and Null means the appointment wasn't evaluated.

This column tracks the version of the logic used for our "Could Have Been Scheduled Online Items" in I EPT 28156, I EPT 28158, and I EPT 28162. If this item is not populated, then the contact has a default value of 1 indicating the initial version.  If one of the above items has a change in it's logic, then a new version will be created here. Notably, changes in logic can be item-specific, so older versions can still be up-to-date for the unaffected items.

Indicates whether the appointment for this patient could have been scheduled online through Open Scheduling. Yes (11) indicates the appointment would have been available, No (12) means it wouldn't have been available, Not Applicable (13) means the appointment didn't meet qualifications to check, and Null means the appointment wasn't evaluated.

Indicates whether the appointment for this patient could have been scheduled online through Ticket Scheduling. Yes (11) indicates the appointment would have been available, No (12) means it wouldn't have been available, Not Applicable (13) means the appointment didn't meet qualifications to check, and Null means the appointment wasn't evaluated.
The unique ID of the visit coverage associated with the appointment.
The ID of the department for the encounter. If there are multiple departments for the encounter, this is the ID of the first department in the list.
The status of the eCheck-In for this appointment.

The date and time when the patient was first assigned to a room for an appointment.  This column is only populated for outpatient appointments where the "Room Patient" button is used for room assignment.  This is distinct from roomed times as calculated by clinical timestamps and the Arrival List.
The unique ID of the hospital account associated with the appointment.

For Hospital Outpatient Visit (HOV) encounters, this column stores the unique contact serial number for the patient contact which is used for clinical documentation.  This can be set for appointment contacts if they are not converted to HOVs.
Indicates whether or not the appointment is a joint appointment. Y indicates that it is a joint appointment, and N indicates that it is not.

This item is a flag for an appointment that is a late cancel. A late cancel occurs when an appointment is canceled with insufficient time to use that time for another patient. For most organizations, late cancels are operationally considered to be a no show.
The number of calls made to the patient about the appointment using communication tracking functionality.
The date and time that the nurse left the room.

Indicates whether or not the appointment was booked into an overbook opening. Y indicates that the appointment was overbooked. N indicates that the appointment was not overbooked. If this is a joint appointment, Y will indicate that the appointment was overbooked with at least one of the providers.

Indicates whether or not the appointment was scheduled outside of the template. Y indicates that it was scheduled outside of the template, and N indicates that it was not. If this is a joint appointment, this column will have Y if it is outside of the regular schedule for at least one of the providers.
The date and time that the patient was paged after checking in for their appointment.
The unique contact serial number for this appointment. This number is unique across all patient encounters in your system. If you use IntraConnect, this is the Unique Contact Identifier (UCI).
The unique ID assigned to the patient record. This ID may be encrypted if you have elected to use enterprise reporting’s encryption utility.
This column displays whether or not the appointment was initially scheduled online, determined by the auditing source application.
The MyChart status when the appointment was scheduled.
The category number for the status returned from an automated appointment reminder system.
The date and time that the physician entered the room.
The unique ID of the visit type for the appointment.
The unique ID of the appointment provider. This is frequently used to join to the CLARITY_SER table. For joint appointments, this contains the ID of the primary provider on the appointment.
The unique ID of the referral attached to the appointment.

Indicates whether or not the appointment requires a referral as determined by the visit coverage and appointment information. Y indicates that a referral is required. N indicates that a referral is not required.
The unique ID of the referring provider for this appointment. This column is frequently used to join to the CLARITY_SER table.
The contact serial number of the non-canceled appointment rescheduled from the appointment.
